events.title: Hilbert and Ackermann pose the Entscheidungsproblem
events.summary: David [Hilbert] and Wilhelm Ackermann's 1928 textbook Grundzüge der theoretischen Logik gave the canonical statement of the [Entscheidungsproblem] — whether an algorithm can decide if any logical formula is universally valid.
events.about: The decision problem asked whether truth in first-order logic could be mechanized. Church and [Turing] answered no in 1936; [Gödel] had already shown completeness of first-order logic in 1929. This 1928 text is the challenge statement that launched computability theory.

narrative.whyChosen: The [Entscheidungsproblem] is the explicit question Church and [Turing] proved unanswerable.
narrative.whyImportant: It turned philosophy-of-mathematics into a concrete problem about algorithms.
narrative.problemSolved: Logicians lacked a precise target for what 'mechanical proof' should mean.
